paragraphs.title: A Plea for Judgment and Rescue

answers: God
The enemy
The deceitful man
easy.explanation: The verse begins, "Judge me, O God."
easy.q: To whom does the psalmist appeal for judgment?

answers: From the holy hill
From the deceitful and unjust man
From the harp
easy.explanation: He asks God to deliver him from "the deceitful and unjust man."
easy.q: From whom does the psalmist ask to be delivered?

answers: Plead his cause
Lead him to the tabernacles
Teach him to play the harp
easy.explanation: He asks God to "plead my cause against an ungodly nation."
easy.q: What does the psalmist ask God to do concerning his cause?

answers: Because he is facing an ungodly nation
Because he wants to reach the holy hill
Because he wants to praise with the harp
medium.explanation: The request is made against "an ungodly nation."
medium.q: Why does the psalmist ask God to plead his cause?

answers: Not revering or honoring God
Skilled at playing music
Living on the holy hill
medium.explanation: An ungodly nation is one that does not honor or follow God.
medium.q: What does "ungodly" mean in this verse?

answers: Judgment, defense, and deliverance
Harp-playing, mourning, and abandonment
A holy hill, an enemy, and a tabernacle
medium.explanation: He asks God to judge him, plead his cause, and deliver him from evil.
medium.q: Which sequence best describes the psalmist's requests?

answers: God is viewed as the psalmist's defender
God is described as a musician
God causes the psalmist to mourn
challenge.explanation: The psalmist asks God to act on his behalf as an advocate and protector.
challenge.q: What does the request to have God plead the psalmist's cause suggest about God?

answers: Light and truth
Deceitful and unjust
Holy and joyful
challenge.explanation: The man is described as both deceitful and unjust.
challenge.q: Which pair names the two kinds of wrongdoing mentioned in the verse?

answers: The psalmist asks for both a right judgment and rescue from the wrongdoer
The psalmist is choosing between judgment and music
The psalmist is asking to leave the holy hill
challenge.explanation: He seeks justice in his case and protection from the person harming him.
challenge.q: How are "judge me" and "deliver me" related in the verse?

paragraphs.title: A Sense of Abandonment and the Enemy's Pressure

answers: As his strength
As his altar
As his harp
easy.explanation: He says, "thou art the God of my strength."
easy.q: How does the psalmist describe God?

answers: The oppression of the enemy
The joy of praise
The light and truth
easy.explanation: He asks why he goes mourning because of "the oppression of the enemy."
easy.q: What causes the psalmist to go mourning?

answers: Why dost thou cast me off?
Who will play the harp?
Where are the tabernacles?
easy.explanation: The psalmist asks, "why dost thou cast me off?"
easy.q: What question does the psalmist ask God?

answers: God is called his strength, yet he feels cast off
He is joyful but refuses to praise
He is already at the holy hill but wants to leave
medium.explanation: The psalmist trusts God as his strength while still feeling abandoned.
medium.q: How do confidence and distress appear together in the verse?

answers: To walk in grief and sadness
To go joyfully to the altar
To play music loudly
medium.explanation: The phrase describes walking in sorrow because of oppression.
medium.q: What does "go mourning" mean in this context?

answers: The oppression of the enemy
His longing for the harp
His desire to reach the holy hill
medium.explanation: He directly connects his mourning with the enemy's oppression.
medium.q: What reason does the psalmist give for his mourning?

answers: God is his strength, yet he feels abandoned
Music is opposed to sacrifice
Light is opposed to truth
challenge.explanation: The verse combines trust in God with the painful feeling of being cast off.
challenge.q: What is the central tension in this verse?

answers: The psalmist is trying to understand his suffering
The psalmist has decided to praise God
The psalmist is describing a sacred place
challenge.explanation: The questions express confusion about his difficult condition.
challenge.q: What do the questions about being cast off and going mourning reveal?

answers: He is presently under pressure from an enemy
He has already reached the altar
He is playing the harp
challenge.explanation: The verse describes the enemy's oppression as an immediate cause of his mourning.
challenge.q: Which important detail about the psalmist's condition appears in the verse?

answers: His light and truth
Enemies and deceit
Mourning and oppression
easy.explanation: He asks, "O send out thy light and thy truth."
easy.q: What does the psalmist ask God to send?

answers: To the house of the unjust man
To God's holy hill and tabernacles
To a place of oppression
easy.explanation: He asks that they bring him to God's holy hill and tabernacles.
easy.q: Where will the light and truth lead the psalmist?

answers: Upon the harp
By pleading his cause
By hiding from the enemy
easy.explanation: He says, "upon the harp will I praise thee."
easy.q: How will the psalmist praise God?

answers: They guide the psalmist toward God's presence
They increase the enemy's oppression
They keep him away from the altar
medium.explanation: The psalmist asks them to lead and bring him to the holy place.
medium.q: What role do light and truth have in these verses?

answers: His dwelling places
Deceitful people
Musical instruments
medium.explanation: The tabernacles refer to places associated with God's dwelling and presence.
medium.q: What are God's "tabernacles" in this context?

answers: Light and truth, arrival at the holy place, praise with the harp
Harp, oppression, and abandonment
Injustice, mourning, and separation from God
medium.explanation: God's light and truth lead the psalmist to worship and praise.
medium.q: Which sequence best describes the movement in these verses?

answers: Guidance toward God's presence leads to worship and joy
Guidance causes the psalmist to move away from God
Praise prevents him from reaching the holy hill
challenge.explanation: The path led by light and truth ends in worship before God.
challenge.q: How are the guidance in verse 3 and the praise in verse 4 connected?

answers: As the psalmist's exceeding joy
As a deceitful and unjust man
As the enemy who oppresses him
challenge.explanation: The psalmist calls God "my exceeding joy."
challenge.q: How is God described in verse 4?

answers: The psalmist seeks to move from need and guidance to nearness and praise
The psalmist wants to remain under enemy oppression
The psalmist is abandoning fellowship with God
challenge.explanation: Coming to the altar represents drawing near to God in worship.
challenge.q: What can be understood from the movement toward God's altar?

answers: His soul
His enemy
His harp
easy.explanation: He addresses himself by asking, "O my soul."
easy.q: To whom does the psalmist speak in this verse?

answers: Hope in God
Mourn under oppression
Hide from the truth
easy.explanation: He commands his soul, "hope in God."
easy.q: What does the psalmist tell his soul to do?

answers: Praise God
Argue with God
Leave the altar
easy.explanation: He says, "I shall yet praise him."
easy.q: What does the psalmist say he will yet do?

answers: Because he believes he will yet praise God
Because he wants to escape from God
Because the enemy has already won
medium.explanation: His hope is grounded in the expectation that he will praise God again.
medium.q: Why does the psalmist encourage his soul to hope in God?

answers: Why are you discouraged and bowed down?
Why are you playing music?
Why are you climbing the holy hill?
medium.explanation: To be cast down describes a condition of discouragement and inner heaviness.
medium.q: What does "Why art thou cast down, O my soul?" mean?

answers: Because the soul is troubled, the psalmist calls it to trust God
Because the soul is joyful, he commands it to grieve
Because the soul is playing music, he commands it to be silent
medium.explanation: The psalmist responds to inner distress by directing his soul toward hope.
medium.q: What connection exists between the soul's condition and the command to hope?

answers: His faith that God is his salvation and his God
The knowledge that the enemy has disappeared
His desire to approach an unjust man
challenge.explanation: He can hope because he identifies God as his salvation and his God.
challenge.q: What enables the psalmist to move from questioning to encouragement?

answers: He expects to praise God again in the future
He has permanently stopped praising God
He will never praise God
challenge.q: What does the word "yet" communicate in "I shall yet praise him"?

answers: It gives hope after the experience of abandonment and oppression
It cancels the request for deliverance
It introduces another deceitful man
challenge.explanation: After describing distress, the psalmist strengthens himself with hope in God.
challenge.q: How does verse 5 relate to the earlier verses?
